notes: A handwritten continuation list gives 17 correction entries for referenced pages 41 through 90. There is no title, date, author signature, internal page number, or total page count. The lower-left 17 is an archive numeral.
The first entry corrects asperic to aspheric and adds the French asperges aside. Later entries correct denote/debote, of/ob, Assume/Asumme and several misplaced apostrophes.

At p.66 line 13 the writer asks whether compositum (singular), composita (plural) is preferable to composita, compositae, says they are no Latin expert, and says the dictionary is not goodenough to be sure. Preserve the question and uncertainty.

At p.89 line 8 the writer asks whether very is necessary. At line -15 they offer last but not least and last, not least, as alternatives. The p.42 and p.89 preferences are qualified as more usual/more usually.

At P.90 line -15 the writer says compare takes with, as does commute, reporting 4 occurences on the referenced page. At line -8 they propose replacing a comma by that for a better flow of words. The number 4 is the writer's report about another page, not a count verified here.

The dictionary qualification retains the spacing doubt goodenough/good enough. Capitalization in both Latin occurrences and in the first proposed Compositum/compositum is unresolved. These are ink questions; no Latin grammar or historical assertion was independently checked. Three underlined spans, the opening cancellation, all seventeen entries and the archive number are included.
